title: EGCG, GCG, TFDG, or TSA Inhibiting Melanin Synthesis by Downregulating MC1R Expression.
authors: Wang, Wei; Di, Taimei; Wang, Weiwei; Jiang, Heyuan
one_liner_zh: 该文研究茶多酚抑制黑色素合成，涉及MC1R蛋白的分子对接，但核心是细胞表型与基因表达，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法。
abstract: Without affecting cell viability, epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), gallocatechin gallate (GCG), theaflavine-3,3'-digallate (TFDG), or theasinensin A (TSA) have been found to effectively reduce intracellular melanin content and tyrosinase (TYR) activity. However, studies on the anti-melanogenic mechanism of the above samples remain weak, and the activities of these samples in regulating melanogenesis at the molecular level lack comparison. Using B16F10 cells with the alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH) stimulation and without the alpha-MSH stimulation as models, the effects of EGCG, GCG, TFDG, or TSA on cell phenotypes and expression of key targets related to melanogenesis were studied. The results showed that alpha-MSH always promoted melanogenesis with or without adding the four samples. Meanwhile, the anti-melanogenic activities of the four samples were not affected by whether the alpha-MSH was added in the medium or not and the added time of the alpha-MSH. On this basis, the 100 microg/mL EGCG, GCG, TFDG, or TSA did not affect the TYR catalytic activity but inhibited melanin formation partly through downregulating the melanocortin 1 receptor (MC1R), microphthalmia-associated transcription factor (MITF), and the TYR family. The downregulation abilities of catechins on the TYR family and MITF expression were stronger than those of dimers at both the transcription and translation levels, while the ability of dimers to downregulate the MC1R expression was stronger than that of catechins at both the transcription and translation levels to some extent. The results of molecular docking showed that these four samples could stably bind to MC1R protein. Taken together, this study offered molecular mechanisms for the anti-melanogenic activity of the EGCG, GCG, TFDG, and TSA, as potential effective components against the UV-induced tanning reactions, and a key target (MC1R) was identified.
abstract_zh: 在不影响细胞活力的前提下，表没食子儿茶素没食子酸酯（EGCG）、没食子儿茶素没食子酸酯（GCG）、茶黄素-3,3'-二没食子酸酯（TFDG）或茶黄素A（TSA）已被发现能有效降低细胞内黑色素含量和酪氨酸酶（TYR）活性。然而，关于上述样品抗黑色素生成机制的研究仍较薄弱，且这些样品在分子水平上调节黑色素生成的活性缺乏比较。以经α-黑素细胞刺激激素（alpha-MSH）刺激和未经alpha-MSH刺激的B16F10细胞为模型，研究了EGCG、GCG、TFDG或TSA对细胞表型及与黑色素生成相关关键靶点表达的影响。结果表明，无论是否添加这四种样品，alpha-MSH总是促进黑色素生成。同时，这四种样品的抗黑色素生成活性不受培养基中是否添加alpha-MSH及alpha-MSH添加时间的影响。在此基础上，100微克/毫升的EGCG、GCG、TFDG或TSA不影响TYR催化活性，但部分通过下调黑皮质素1受体（MC1R）、小眼畸形相关转录因子（MITF）和TYR家族来抑制黑色素形成。儿茶素类对TYR家族和MITF表达的下调能力在转录和翻译水平上均强于二聚体类，而二聚体类下调MC1R表达的能力在转录和翻译水平上在一定程度上强于儿茶素类。分子对接结果显示，这四种样品能稳定结合MC1R蛋白。综上所述，本研究为EGCG、GCG、TFDG和TSA的抗黑色素生成活性提供了分子机制，这些化合物作为对抗紫外线诱导晒黑反应的潜在有效成分，并识别了一个关键靶点（MC1R）。
